column2: On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in what he relates from his Lord, Blessed and Exalted is He, who said: “Allah has written down the good deeds and the bad deeds, and then He made that clear. Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, Allah writes it down with Himself as a complete good deed;
and if he intends it and does it, Allah writes it down with Himself as ten good deeds, up to seven hundred times, up to many times more.

And if he intends a bad deed but does not do it, Allah writes it down with Himself as a complete good deed; and if he intends it and does it, Allah writes it down as a single bad deed.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim in their two Ṣaḥīḥs with these words.
Tabāraka (“Blessed is He”): exalted in greatness.
Wa-taʿālā (“and Exalted”): far above what does not befit His perfection.
“Has written down the good deeds and the bad deeds”: has decreed them in His knowledge in accordance with what will occur.
“Then He made that clear”: to the recording angels.
“Allah writes it down”: for the one who intended it; that is, He commands the guardian angels to write it.
“A complete good deed”: with no deficiency in it, even though it arose from intention alone.
Ḍiʿf (“times”): with kasrah on the ḍād; a like, and it has been said, twice the like.
“Up to many times more”: according to the increase in sincerity, truthfulness of resolve, presence of heart and the extent to which its benefit reaches others.
“A single bad deed”: out of His favour, Glorified is He, since He does not take His servant to account for merely intending a bad deed, nor multiply it against him after it has been done.
An explanation of Allah's great favour to this nation; were it not for what is mentioned in the hadith, the calamity would be great, because the servants do more bad deeds [than good].
The guardian angels record the deeds of the hearts, contrary to those who say they record only outward deeds.
Intending a good deed is written as a complete good deed.
Whoever intends a good deed and does it, Allah writes it down with Himself as ten good deeds, unless He wills more than that.

Intending a bad deed without doing it is written as a good deed; but the leaving that is rewarded is leaving it while able to do it, for the Face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because some narrations of this hadith have: “…he left it only on My account.”

A bad deed is written as its like without multiplication; this does not contradict its being made graver by the sanctity of the time and place, or by the strength of the doer's knowledge of Allah and his nearness to Him.
The multiplication is not limited to seven hundred.
The printed text reads إذ لو ما ذكر, evidently for إذ لولا ما ذكر (“were it not for what is mentioned”).
